title: test(electron): 引入可复用的 E2E 测试 Harness 和冒烟测试
body:
## Problem

The repository has a well-established Vitest/jsdom suite, but the Electron Demo has no end-to-end automation boundary. Renderer-level tests cannot validate Electron main/renderer integration, native-dialog handling, real file persistence, or complete user workflows.

## Solution

This PR introduces a reusable Playwright Electron E2E harness for the Electron Demo.

- Reusable Electron fixture that launches the built `dist-electron/main.js` entry point.
- Isolated temporary workspace and Electron `user-data-dir` for every test.
- Renderer diagnostics for `console.error` and `pageerror`, plus Electron stderr capture.
- Failure artifacts: Playwright trace, screenshot, HTML report, and attached Electron diagnostics.
- A dedicated GitHub Actions E2E job running under `xvfb-run` on Ubuntu 24.04.
- A test-only `NEXUS_E2E=1` guard around the main-process native dialog stub.

## Covered workflows

- Application launch and accessible Markdown editor readiness.
- Markdown editing with undo and redo assertions.
- File lifecycle: open, edit, save, verify persisted contents with Node `fs.readFile`, modify on disk, and reopen through the application.

## Running locally

```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm build
pnpm build:electron-demo
pnpm test:e2e
```

## CI and failure diagnostics

E2E runs in an independent CI job. On failure, GitHub Actions uploads `apps/electron-demo/playwright-report/` and `apps/electron-demo/test-results/`; the harness retains screenshots, traces, and Electron diagnostics without relying on fixed waits or retries.

## Dependency

- `@playwright/test@1.61.1` — Apache-2.0 — development-only dependency for Electron E2E execution; locked in `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

## AI assistance

AI tools were used to assist with harness design, implementation iteration, and code review. The contributor reviewed the final scope and validation results.

## Validation

The following checks passed locally:

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm test`
- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm build:electron-demo`
- `pnpm test:e2e` — 10 consecutive passing runs (3 tests per run)

## Compliance

- [ ] CLA signed — awaiting the repository's first-time contributor flow.
- [x] New dependency documented with license and rationale.
- [x] No build artifacts, test reports, secrets, or personal data committed.
- [x] No public runtime API change; no OpenSpec proposal required.

## Screenshots / recordings

Not applicable: this change adds automated test infrastructure rather than a user-visible product change.

@@ -0,0 +1,27 @@
+# Electron E2E tests
+
+The suite launches the packaged Electron main process from
+`dist-electron/main.js`; it does not use a Vite development server. It covers
+the critical editor path: application startup, Markdown editing with undo/redo,
+and opening, saving, and reopening a Markdown file.
+
+Run the tests from the repository root:
+
+```bash
+pnpm build
+pnpm build:electron-demo
+pnpm test:e2e
+```
+
+Each test receives an isolated Electron user-data directory and temporary
+workspace. Native file dialogs are stubbed in the Electron main process, so
+the file lifecycle test uses real file IO without depending on an operating
+system dialog. The fixture captures renderer console errors and preserves
+Playwright traces and screenshots when a test fails.
+
+The suite launches the Electron binary supplied by the `electron` dependency;
+it does not download or launch a separate Playwright browser.
+
+The Playwright Electron API is experimental. After upgrading `@playwright/test`,
+rerun the full E2E suite and validate the GitHub Actions job before relying on
+the upgrade.

+import { defineConfig } from "@playwright/test";
+import path from "node:path";
+
+const outputDir = path.resolve(__dirname, "test-results");
+const reportDir = path.resolve(__dirname, "playwright-report");
+
+export default defineConfig({
+  testDir: "./e2e",
+  testMatch: "**/*.spec.ts",
+  outputDir,
+  timeout: 30_000,
+  expect: {
+    timeout: 5_000,
+  },
+  fullyParallel: false,
+  workers: 1,
+  retries: 0,
+  reporter: [
+    ["list"],
+    ["html", { open: "never", outputFolder: reportDir }],
+  ],
+  use: {
+    screenshot: "only-on-failure",
+    trace: "retain-on-failure",
+  },
+});
